reasons: Depends on seven components that were not reviewed here.

terms.meaning: a reusable piece of a page, written as a tag such as Hero
the page area that holds the main content, read by screen readers as the core of the page

used_by: Next.js routes the site's root address to this file

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Section imports
sections.what: Brings in the navigation and each of the seven page sections.
sections.why: Each section lives in its own component so it can be edited separately.
sections.watch_out: A renamed or moved component file breaks this import and the whole home page.

sections.name: Home
sections.title: Sections in reading order
sections.what: Shows the navigation, then the sections in order from the hero down to the contact area.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single scrolling page where the order tells the story.
sections.watch_out: Moving a section changes the scroll story and any anchor links that point to it.

summary: The home page: shows the navigation and then the main sections in a fixed order.
purpose: Presents the whole one-page portfolio: hero, AI builds, experience, atlas invite, curiosities, about and contact.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The sections are listed in one place, so their order is easy to change.
how: 1) Renders the top navigation. 2) Inside the main area, shows the sections in order: hero, AI builds, experience journey, atlas invite, curiosities, about, contact.
inputs: None. The page reads no props or data directly.
risks: Each section is a separate component. If one breaks, the page may break too; no error boundary is visible in this file.
debug: If a section is missing, check its import at the top and that it is listed in the main area. If the order is wrong, reorder the list in the main area.
